summary:
Subcarpathian (Podkarpackie) is the epicentre and last holdout of Poland's "LGBT-ideology-free" resolution wave. It was one of five voivodeships adopting a regional anti-LGBT declaration (repealed 20 September 2021 only after the European Commission threatened to freeze its regional development funds), and its Łańcut county held Poland's final surviving anti-LGBT charter of the family until its extraordinary-session repeal on 24 April 2025—six years after the phenomenon began. The capital, Rzeszów, saw its mayor Tadeusz Ferenc outright ban the 2019 Equality March on security grounds; the district court later overturned the ban and the march proceeded, but the executive intent to exclude a visible LGBTQ public presence is on the record.

The resolutions were never criminal statutes, but the repeal was extrinsic (EU funding leverage) rather than a change in local attitudes, meaning the de facto social climate that produced them persists. For a visitor, the practical exposure is being visibly trans at a public event in an eastern Podkarpackie town where the local authority resisted all external pressure until 2025.

Score of 0.42 sits 0.10 below the national 0.52. Well below Łódź (0.48), which also carried a voivodeship-level resolution but produced neither a march ban nor a five-year institutional holdout. This is the deepest sub-national negative in Poland's dossier.

sources.summary: English-language Poland monitoring outlet (27 Apr 2025): the Lanicki county (powiat lancucki) assembly, at an extraordinary session with the single item on its agenda, repealed Poland's final remaining anti-LGBT resolution - six years after the 'LGBT-ideology-free' wave began; the last-holdout fact behind this region's deviation.

LGBTQ-news report (2021): the Subcarpathian voivodeship sejmik withdrew its 'anti-LGBT ideology' declaration after the European Commission threatened to freeze regional development funds - evidence the repeal was externally driven rather than an attitudinal shift.

Regional news (Polish, 2019): the district court in Rzeszow overturned the city mayor's ban on the second Equality March, ruling the march could proceed; the mayor said he would not appeal - the judicial reversal of an executive attempt to exclude a visible LGBTQ public event.

National legal-current-affairs daily (Polish, 2019): mayor Tadeusz Ferenc banned the Rzeszow equality parade citing police-safety consultations; the regional left called the decision undemocratic - the executive intent to exclude, on the record.

Reference article mapping the whole 'LGBT-free zone' phenomenon by tier - voivodeships (provinces), counties (powiats) and municipalities - listing Podkarpackie among the five voivodeships that adopted declarations and documenting the EU-funding pressure and repeal timeline across the wave.
